title: Ordinary etale adjoint on strict coefficient systems
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and a uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and write $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type schemes over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type morphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; $Y$ need not be separated over $k$. Fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For a scheme $T$, use the category $\mathsf S_A(T_{\mathrm{et}})$ of strict varying-coefficient systems and its derived category defined in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. On this category $j_{!,A}$ means termwise extension by zero and $p_{A,*}$ means termwise ordinary etale direct image, and put $F_{f,A}=Rp_{A,*}j_{!,A}$.

The functor $F_{f,A}:D(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))\to D(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$ has an $O$-linear exact right adjoint $G_{f,A}$ on these unbounded derived categories of systems. For every $n$ there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e_nG_{f,A}M\cong f_n^\times(e_nM),$$
where $f_n^\times$ is the ordinary etale right adjoint at $A_n$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The comparisons identify the evaluated units, counits and transition maps with their adjunction mates at the finite coefficient levels. There is an integer $c_f\geq0$, independent of $n$, such that $G_{f,A}$ sends $D^{\geq a}(\mathsf S_A(Y_{\mathrm{et}}))$ into $D^{\geq a-c_f}(\mathsf S_A(X_{\mathrm{et}}))$ for every integer $a$. It sends every bounded-below normalized system to a bounded-below normalized system, with normalization as explicitly defined in [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison]. These assertions are for actual functors and natural transformations in the derived category of strict coefficient systems, including their map action and independence of complex resolutions.

For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ with $O'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, use the coefficient system $B_n=O'/\varpi^nO'$ and the exact levelwise extension of scalars $T_{B/A}$ (each $B_n$ is finite free over $A_n$). The canonical scalar comparison is an isomorphism of functors of derived systems
$$T_{B/A}G_{f,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{f,B}T_{B/A}.$$
Here $G_{f,B}$ is the same right-adjoint construction with $O'$ and the non-zero-divisor $\varpi$; normalization is relative to its powers. These comparisons respect the identity extension and composition, quotient maps and the canonical tensor associators. If $\varpi'$ is a uniformizer of $O'$ and $e$ is the ramification index, $\varpi^nO'=(\varpi')^{en}O'$, so restriction to these levels is the cofinal subsequence of the system indexed by powers of $\varpi'$. Restricting the construction to that subsequence agrees with the construction just stated, including its maps. No inverse limit, completed integral output, constructible restriction or pro-etale exceptional adjoint is asserted in this lemma.

source.place: Constructions 5.14–5.15, Lemma 5.16 and the Brown adjoint following it (printed pp. 34–35); Lemma 5.22 and Proposition 5.24 (printed pp. 36–37), with the bounded-below equivalence of normalization conditions in Lemma 4.13 (printed p. 24). The finite-free scalar comparison is the finite-free instance of the tensor/adjunction construction in Proposition 2.29(2) and its system version in Construction 5.15; cofinal indexing uses Construction 4.1. The bound c_f follows from the finite cohomological amplitude [0,2d] in Construction 5.15 by adjunction.
